name: centered-wordmark
text: FACT CHECK

name: opening-tagline
text: Verify what you read.
Have you ever read a news article and stopped to wonder: is this actually true? That question is why I built Fact Check.

name: header-wordmark
text: FACT CHECK

name: ai-question
text:
Why not just use
ChatGPT or Claude?
textPreview: Why not just use | ChatGPT or Claude?

text: General AI tools can browse and cite sources. But they are open-ended assistants. Fact Check is built around one repeatable verification workflow.

name: header-wordmark
text: FACT CHECK

name: evidence-statement
text:
A confident answer is not
the same as verified evidence.
textPreview: A confident answer is not | the same as verified evidence.

name: evidence-subtitle
text: Fact Check shows the claim, the reasoning, and the sources.
textPreview: Fact Check shows the claim, the reasoning, and the sources.

text: Instead of asking you to engineer a prompt, the platform separates claims, searches for evidence, evaluates each source, and keeps the result inspectable.

name: header-wordmark
text: FACT CHECK

name: product-headline
text:
Fact-check any article
without leaving the page.
textPreview: Fact-check any article | without leaving the page.

name: product-subtitle
text: Open the extension. Check the page. Review the evidence.
textPreview: Open the extension. Check the page. Review the evidence.

alt: Fact Check extension reviewing an article beside the browser page

text:
Fact Check works inside the browser. It reads the article, identifies factual claims, and returns the results beside the original content.

text: FACT CHECK

text: PASTE ANY TEXT

name: input-subtitle
text: The same evidence workflow for every mode.
textPreview: The same evidence workflow for every mode.

text: Users can check the page already open in Chrome, paste an article URL, or paste any paragraph directly.

name: header-wordmark
text: FACT CHECK

name: verdict-title
text: Every claim gets an honest outcome.
textPreview: Every claim gets an honest outcome.

name: true
text: TRUE

name: false
text: FALSE

name: unverifiable
text: UNVERIFIABLE
The platform uses three clear outcomes: true, false, or unverifiable. It does not pretend that every question has a decisive answer.

name: header-wordmark
text: FACT CHECK

name: pipeline-title
text: Evidence comes before the verdict.

name: pipeline
text: ARTICLE   →   CLAIMS   →   SOURCES   →   VERDICT

name: pipeline-subtitle
text: Each source is checked against its own claim.
textPreview: Each source is checked against its own claim.

text: The system extracts factual claims, searches for evidence, evaluates each source, and only then derives the final verdict.

name: header-wordmark
text: FACT CHECK

name: no-evidence
text:
No evidence?
No verdict.

name: no-evidence-subtitle
text: When sources are missing or conflicting, Fact Check says so.
textPreview: When sources are missing or conflicting, Fact Check says so.

text: A safe verification system must be able to say that the available evidence is not enough. Honest uncertainty is better than fabricated confidence.

name: header-wordmark
text: FACT CHECK

name: review-title
text:
Review the reasoning.
Open the sources.
Export the report.
textPreview: Review the reasoning. | Open the sources. | Export the report.

name: review-subtitle
text: The result stays useful after the check is complete.
textPreview: The result stays useful after the check is complete.

alt: Fact Check verdict with reasoning and cited evidence

text:
Every result keeps the claim, explanation, and sources together. Users can open the evidence directly or export the review as Markdown or JSON.

name: centered-wordmark
text: FACT CHECK

name: closing-line
text: Read. Question. Verify.
The next time you wonder whether something online is true, you should be able to verify it where you found it. That is Fact Check.
